name: Col' Spring Glen
facts: Described as no healthy nor decent place
Whippoorwills and fireflies there never act like creatures of God
Strange sounds could be heard rushing and talking in the air there between the rock falls and Bear's Den
Whatever burst loose upon the world had gone down into the great sinister ravine
All the trees on the banks were bent and broken and a great avenue had been gouged in the underbrush
Only a distant fetor came from below, no sound
Three dogs seemed cowed and reluctant when near the glen
Elmer Frye's house was on the eastern edge of Cold Spring Glen
Monstrous tracks seemed to argue a passage in two directions between Cold Spring Glen and Sentinel Hill
The Frye place stood at the head of the glen and was destroyed

sources.quote: I allus says Col' Spring Glen ain't no healthy nor decent place. The whippoorwills an' fireflies there never did act like they was creaters o' Gawd, an' they's them as says ye kin hear strange things a-rushin' an' a-talkin' in the air daown thar ef ye stand in the right place, atween the rock falls an' Bear's Den.

Whatever had burst loose upon the world had assuredly gone down into the great sinister ravine; for all the trees on the banks were bent and broken, and a great avenue had been gouged in the precipice-hanging underbrush.
a frightful stench and the savage barking of the dogs awakened the household at Elmer Frye's, on the eastern edge of Cold Spring Glen
as if the moving mountain had come from Cold Spring Glen and returned to it along the same path
a hastily assembled group of armed men trudged out to the Frye place at the head of the glen

name: Bear's Den
facts: Strange sounds could be heard in the air near this landmark within Cold Spring Glen

sources.quote: they's them as says ye kin hear strange things a-rushin' an' a-talkin' in the air daown thar ef ye stand in the right place, atween the rock falls an' Bear's Den

name: Dunwich
facts: Three-quarters of the men and boys of Dunwich trooped between the Whateley ruins and Cold Spring Glen
The editor of the Aylesbury Transcript was accustomed to wild tales from Dunwich
The next day all the countryside was in a panic
The Elmer Fryes had been erased from Dunwich

sources.quote: By that noon fully three-quarters of the men and boys of Dunwich were trooping over the roads and meadows between the new-made Whateley ruins and Cold Spring Glen
The Elmer Fryes had been erased from Dunwich.

name: Aylesbury
facts: The Aylesbury Transcript published a humorous item about the tracks
Earl Sawyer suggested that help be asked from Aylesbury

sources.quote: Someone telephoned the news to the Aylesbury Transcript; but the editor, accustomed to wild tales from Dunwich, did no more than concoct a humorous paragraph about it
Earl Sawyer suggested that help be asked from Aylesbury or Arkham, but others maintained it would be of no use.

name: Arkham
facts: Earl Sawyer suggested that help be asked from Arkham
The manuscript diary of Wilbur Whateley was being studied behind a closed door of a shelf-lined room in Arkham
The manuscript had been delivered to Miskatonic University for translation

sources.quote: Earl Sawyer suggested that help be asked from Aylesbury or Arkham, but others maintained it would be of no use.
a quieter yet even more spiritually poignant phase of the horror had been blackly unwinding itself behind the closed door of a shelf-lined room in Arkham

name: Miskatonic University
facts: The manuscript diary of Wilbur Whateley was delivered there for translation
Experts in ancient and modern languages there were puzzled by the manuscript's alphabet

sources.quote: The curious manuscript record or diary of Wilbur Whateley, delivered to Miskatonic University for translation, had caused much worry and bafflement among the experts in languages both ancient and modern

name: Sentinel Hill
facts: Fresh monstrous tracks were found in the road skirting Sentinel Hill
A thirty-foot swath of crushed shrubbery led steeply upward from the base of the hill
The horror could scale a sheer stony cliff of almost complete verticality on the hill
The trail ended or reversed at the hill's summit
The Whateleys used to build hellish fires and chant rituals by a table-like stone atop the hill on May Eve and Hallowmass
The stone was found with a thick fetid tarry deposit like that on the ruined Whateley farmhouse floor

sources.quote: early explorers noted with horror a fresh set of the monstrous tracks in the road skirting Sentinel Hill
It was here that the Whateleys used to build their hellish fires and chant their hellish rituals by the table-like stone on May Eve and Hallowmass.

name: Whateley farmhouse
facts: Tarry stickiness was observed on the floor of the ruined farmhouse when the horror escaped
The farmhouse had become a strange noisome wreck

sources.quote: examining in horror the vast, monstrous prints, the maimed Bishop cattle, the strange, noisome wreck of the farmhouse
the same tarry stickiness observed on the floor of the ruined Whateley farmhouse when the horror escaped

name: Frye place
facts: One side of the old red barn had completely caved in
Only about a quarter of the cattle could be found and identified
The house had caved in like an egg-shell and nothing living or dead could be discovered amongst the ruins

sources.quote: one side of the old red barn had completely caved in. Of the cattle, only about a quarter could be found and identified.

There were more swaths and monstrous prints, but there was no longer any house. It had caved in like an egg-shell, and amongst the ruins nothing living or dead could be discovered—only a stench and a tarry stickiness.

name: Mis' Corey
facts: The tracks had not yet reached her house as of the speaker's account

sources.quote: ef they was on the glen rud this side o' the glen, an' ain't got to your haouse yet, I calc'late they must go into the glen itself

name: Luther
facts: He observed the big tracks but it was unclear whether he took account of where they led

sources.quote: Did your Luther take accaount o' whar them big tracks led tew?

name: Elmer Frye
facts: His household was awakened by a stench and barking dogs about 2 in the morning
He lit a lantern through force of habit but knew it would be death to go outside
His family and farm were later destroyed, with the house caved in and no one found
fate: He and his household were erased from Dunwich when their house caved in and nothing living or dead could be found amongst the ruins.

sources.quote: a frightful stench and the savage barking of the dogs awakened the household at Elmer Frye's, on the eastern edge of Cold Spring Glen
Frye lit a lantern through force of habit, but knew it would be death to go out into that black farmyard.
The Elmer Fryes had been erased from Dunwich.

name: Mrs. Frye
facts: She proposed telephoning the neighbors when the noise began

sources.quote: Mrs. Frye proposed telephoning the neighbors, and Elmer was about to agree when the noise of splintering wood burst in upon their deliberations.

name: Selina Frye
facts: She tottered to the telephone and spread news of the second phase of the horror

sources.quote: Selina Frye tottered to the telephone and spread what news she could of the second phase of the horror

name: Earl Sawyer
facts: He suggested that help be asked from Aylesbury or Arkham

sources.quote: Earl Sawyer suggested that help be asked from Aylesbury or Arkham, but others maintained it would be of no use.

name: Old Zebulon Whateley
facts: He was of a branch that hovered about half-way between soundness and decadence
He made darkly wild suggestions about rites that ought to be practised on the hilltops
He came of a line where tradition ran strong, with memories of chantings in the great stone circles connected with Wilbur and his grandfather
He was not with the group at Sentinel Hill and could have done justice to the situation or suggested a plausible explanation

sources.quote: Old Zebulon Whateley, of a branch that hovered about half-way between soundness and decadence, made darkly wild suggestions about rites that ought to be practised on the hilltops.
his memories of chantings in the great stone circles were not altogether connected with Wilbur and his grandfather
Only old Zebulon, who was not with the group, could have done justice to the situation or suggested a plausible explanation.

name: Seth Bishop
facts: His household reported excitement among the dogs and vague sounds and stenches from afar

sources.quote: In the morning both the Frye and the Seth Bishop households reported excitement among the dogs and vague sounds and stenches from afar

name: Dr. Armitage
facts: The old ledger was given wholly into his charge because of his peculiar interest in the Whateley matter and his wide linguistic learning
He had an idea the alphabet might be esoterically used by certain forbidden cults derived from Saracenic wizards
He believed the writer would scarcely have used another speech than his own, so he assumed the manuscript's bulk was in English
He fortified himself with cryptography lore, studying works of Trithemius, Porta, De Vigenere, Falconer, Davys, Thicknesse, Blair, von Marten, and Klüber
He concluded the code of the manuscript was one of great antiquity, handed down through a long line of mystical experimenters
By September he determined that the text was indeed in English

sources.quote: The old ledger was at length given wholly into the charge of Dr. Armitage, both because of his peculiar interest in the Whateley matter, and because of his wide linguistic learning and skill in the mystical formulæ of antiquity and the Middle Ages.

Armitage had an idea that the alphabet might be something esoterically used by certain forbidden cults which have come down from old times, and which have inherited many forms and traditions from the wizards of the Saracenic world.
Armitage concluded that the code of the manuscript was one of great antiquity, no doubt handed down through a long line of mystical experimenters.
it became obvious that the text was indeed in English

name: Wilbur Whateley
facts: His curious manuscript record or diary was delivered to Miskatonic University for translation
Its alphabet caused worry and bafflement among language experts, resembling heavily shaded Arabic used in Mesopotamia but otherwise unknown

sources.quote: The curious manuscript record or diary of Wilbur Whateley, delivered to Miskatonic University for translation, had caused much worry and bafflement among the experts in languages both ancient and modern
